A caustic by itself is unproblematic. For instance, the boundary of the future of two spacelike separated points is the union of two future light cones with the interior parts of the intersection removed. Caustics occur where the light cones intersect, but no singularity lies there.
As a result, the closed trapped null surface has to be compact.
The boundary of the future of the closed trapped null surface is generated by null geodesic segments originating from the surface with tangent vectors orthogonal to it.
A continuous injective map can't create a boundary, giving us our contradiction.
The null geodesics generating the closed trapped null surface have to terminate, however, i.e. reach their future endpoints at or before the caustics.
Consider all such timelike curves passing through the closed trapped null surface and look at their image on the Cauchy surface.
Being a timelike congruence, the timelike curves can't intersect, and so, the map is injective.
Being a continuous injective map, the image also has to be compact.
If the Cauchy surface were noncompact, then the image has a boundary.
But the closed trapped null surface is compact and boundariless because the boundary of a boundary is empty.
